title: Biomechanical Analysis of the Axial Skeleton
question: Explain the structural and mechanical distinctions between the axial and appendicular skeletons. Describe how the curvature of the human vertebral column distributes compressive stress during upright posture.
evaluation_criteria: Accurate differentiation of axial vs appendicular skeletal components
Analysis of cervical, thoracic, and lumbar vertebral curvatures
Biomechanical explanation of shock absorption and load distribution

questions.prompt: Explain the mechanical distribution of stress along the vertebral column and the role of intervertebral discs.
questions.sample_answer: The human spine possesses cervical, thoracic, lumbar, and sacral curves that act like a mechanical spring, distributing axial compressive forces across intervertebral fibrocartilaginous discs to prevent localized fracture.

title: Hemodynamics & Cardiac Cycle Regulation
question: Detail the electrical conduction pathway from the SA node through the Purkinje network, and correlate each phase with the corresponding Wiggers diagram pressure changes during systole and diastole.
evaluation_criteria: Precise pathway: SA node -> AV node -> Bundle of His -> Bundle branches -> Purkinje fibers
Correlation with atrial and ventricular systole/diastole pressure curves
Accurate description of heart valve openings and closures (AV vs semilunar)

questions.prompt: Map out the electrical conduction of the heart and its correlation to ventricular contraction.
questions.sample_answer: Action potentials initiate at the sinoatrial node, traverse internodal pathways to the AV node with a 0.1s delay, then travel down the bundle of His and Purkinje fibers, ensuring coordinated ventricular depolarization from apex to base.

title: Comparative Analysis: Glycolysis vs Oxidative Phosphorylation
question: Compare anaerobic glycolysis and aerobic oxidative phosphorylation in terms of ATP yield per glucose molecule, electron carrier intermediates (NADH/FADH2), and metabolic end products.
evaluation_criteria: Calculation of net ATP yields (2 ATP vs ~30-32 ATP)
Role of mitochondrial cristae and proton gradient generated by complexes I-IV
Evaluation of lactic acid and ethanol fermentation pathways in the absence of oxygen

questions.prompt: Summarize the proton-motive force and ATP synthase mechanism in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
questions.sample_answer: As electrons transfer through complexes I, III, and IV, protons are pumped into the intermembrane space creating an electrochemical gradient that drives ATP synthesis as protons flow back through the F0F1 ATP synthase complex.

title: C3, C4, and CAM Photosynthetic Adaptations
question: Examine how C4 and CAM plant pathways overcome photorespiration caused by RuBisCO oxygenase activity in arid, high-temperature environments.
evaluation_criteria: Explanation of RuBisCO affinity for O2 vs CO2 (photorespiration)
Spatial separation of carbon fixation in C4 (mesophyll vs bundle sheath cells)
Temporal separation of stomatal opening in CAM plants at night

questions.prompt: Differentiate spatial carbon fixation in C4 plants from temporal fixation in CAM plants.
questions.sample_answer: C4 plants spatially separate initial carbon capture (PEP carboxylase in mesophyll) from the Calvin cycle (RuBisCO in bundle sheath), whereas CAM plants temporally separate night-time CO2 uptake into malate from daylight Calvin cycle operations.

title: Born-Haber Cycle & Ionic Lattice Energy
question: Construct the thermochemical Born-Haber cycle for the formation of magnesium oxide (MgO). Detail sublimation enthalpy, ionization energies, bond dissociation energy, electron affinities, and lattice energy.
evaluation_criteria: All thermochemical steps accounted for accurately
Correct signs for endothermic and exothermic transitions
Application of Hess's Law to calculate resultant lattice energy

questions.prompt: Outline the formula and thermodynamic components of the Born-Haber cycle for MgO.
questions.sample_answer: ΔH_formation = ΔH_sub(Mg) + IE1(Mg) + IE2(Mg) + 1/2 ΔH_diss(O2) + EA1(O) + EA2(O) + Lattice Energy.

title: VSEPR Geometry & Hybridization Analysis
question: Determine the steric number, electron-domain geometry, molecular geometry, and central atom hybridization for: SF4, XeF4, and BrF5. Explain deviations from ideal bond angles based on lone pair repulsions.
evaluation_criteria: Steric numbers and hybridizations (sp3d, sp3d2) computed correctly
Accurate identification of lone pair positions in equatorial vs axial positions
Explanation of lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair repulsion hierarchy

questions.prompt: Analyze the molecular shape and bond angles of SF4 using VSEPR theory.
questions.sample_answer: SF4 has 5 electron pairs (4 bonding, 1 lone pair) yielding a see-saw molecular shape with sp3d hybridization. The lone pair occupies an equatorial position minimizing 90-degree repulsions, reducing axial bond angles from 180 to ~173 degrees.

title: Quantum Mechanics & Many-Electron Orbitals
question: State Pauli's Exclusion Principle, Hund's Rule of Maximum Multiplicity, and the Aufbau Principle. Explain the anomalous electron configurations of Chromium (Cr, Z=24) and Copper (Cu, Z=29) based on exchange energy.
evaluation_criteria: Definitions of Pauli, Hund, and Aufbau principles
Electronic configurations: Cr [Ar] 3d5 4s1 and Cu [Ar] 3d10 4s1
Thermodynamic stability of half-filled and completely-filled d-subshells due to exchange energy

questions.prompt: Why does Chromium adopt a [Ar] 3d5 4s1 configuration instead of [Ar] 3d4 4s2?
questions.sample_answer: Chromium promotes one 4s electron to the 3d subshell to achieve a symmetric half-filled 3d5 subshell, which maximizes quantum mechanical electron exchange energy and minimizes electron-electron repulsion.

title: Photoelectric Effect & Wave-Particle Duality
question: Explain Einstein's photoelectric equation: KE_max = hf - Φ. Describe why classical wave theory failed to explain the threshold frequency and instantaneous emission of photoelectrons.
evaluation_criteria: Derivation and variables of Einstein's photoelectric equation
Explanation of work function Φ and cutoff/threshold frequency f0
Contrast with classical continuous wave energy accumulation assumptions

questions.prompt: Why does increasing light intensity not increase the kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons?
questions.sample_answer: Increasing intensity increases the number of photons per second, ejecting more photoelectrons, but photon energy depends solely on frequency (E = hf). Hence, kinetic energy remains unchanged unless frequency increases.

title: Kirchhoff's Laws & Multi-Loop Circuit Solver
question: Formulate the system of linear equations using Kirchhoff's Junction Rule (KCL) and Loop Rule (KVL) for a two-loop circuit with two DC electromotive sources and three branch resistors. Solve for the branch currents.
evaluation_criteria: Statement of conservation of charge (KCL) and conservation of energy (KVL)
Correct sign conventions for potential rises and drops across batteries and resistors
Demonstration of algebraic or matrix solution for branch currents I1, I2, I3

questions.prompt: State Kirchhoff's Current Law and Voltage Law and their underlying physical conservation principles.
questions.sample_answer: KCL states the sum of currents entering a junction equals currents leaving it (Conservation of Charge). KVL states the algebraic sum of potential differences around any closed circuit loop is zero (Conservation of Energy).

title: Dielectrics & Energy Density in Electric Fields
question: Derive the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor filled with a dielectric of constant κ. Explain how atomic polarization within the dielectric reduces the net internal electric field.
evaluation_criteria: Derivation of C = κ ε0 A / d
Analysis of bound surface charge density and induced counter-electric field
Calculation of stored electrostatic energy U = 1/2 C V^2

questions.prompt: Explain how inserting a dielectric increases the capacitance of an isolated charged capacitor.
questions.sample_answer: The external electric field polarizes dielectric atoms, creating opposing surface charges that weaken the net electric field. Because V = Ed, the voltage decreases while charge Q is constant, increasing capacitance C = Q/V by factor κ.

title: Mathematical Modeling of Friction & Braking Distances
question: Derive the formula for the minimum stopping distance of a vehicle of mass m traveling at initial speed v0 on a flat road with kinetic coefficient of friction μk. Prove why stopping distance is independent of vehicle mass.
evaluation_criteria: Work-Energy Theorem or Newton's second law formulation: F_net = -μk m g = m a
Kinematic equation v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a d applied correctly
Result d = v0^2 / (2 μk g) demonstrating that mass m cancels out

questions.prompt: Prove that braking distance d is independent of mass for a skidding vehicle.
questions.sample_answer: Frictional deceleration a = -f/m = -(μk * m * g)/m = -μk * g. From kinematics, 0 = v0^2 - 2(μk g)d, giving d = v0^2 / (2 μk g). Because mass cancels in the acceleration formula, stopping distance depends solely on speed and friction.

title: Stokes' Law & Terminal Velocity in Viscous Fluids
question: Derive the expression for the terminal velocity vt of a spherical ball of radius r and density ρ falling through a viscous fluid of viscosity η and density σ using Stokes' Law (F_drag = 6πηrv).
evaluation_criteria: Free-body diagram balancing gravity, buoyant force, and viscous drag
Equation: m g = F_buoyant + 6πηrv_t
Final algebraic expression: vt = 2 r^2 (ρ - σ) g / (9 η)

questions.prompt: Write the equilibrium force balance equation for a falling sphere at terminal velocity.
questions.sample_answer: At terminal velocity, net acceleration is zero: (4/3)πr^3 ρ g = (4/3)πr^3 σ g + 6πηr vt, yielding vt = 2 r^2 g (ρ - σ) / (9 η).

title: Socioeconomic Repercussions of the First Industrial Revolution
question: Evaluate how the transition from agrarian cottage industries to mechanized factory production between 1760 and 1840 reshaped urban demographic concentrations, child labor policies, and the rise of trade unions.
evaluation_criteria: Analysis of rural-to-urban migration and growth of industrial centers like Manchester
Living and working conditions, working hours, and the Factory Acts of 1833
Evolution of the working class consciousness and early collective bargaining movements

questions.prompt: How did the Factory Act of 1833 address child labor in British textile mills?
questions.sample_answer: The 1833 Act prohibited employment of children under 9 in textile mills, limited working hours for ages 9-13 to 8 hours per day, mandated 2 hours of schooling daily, and established government factory inspectors.

title: Trade Networks & Cultural Diffusion along the Silk Roads
question: Discuss how the trans-Eurasian Silk Road facilitated not merely the commerce of luxury goods (silk, spices, porcelain), but also religious dissemination (Buddhism, Islam), technological transfers (papermaking, gunpowder), and pandemic transmissions.
evaluation_criteria: Specific geographic trade arteries connecting Chang'an, Central Asia, and Mediterranean ports
Transmission of philosophical/religious doctrines and syncretic art
Analysis of technological transmission and biological diffusion (e.g. Black Death)

questions.prompt: Cite two major non-material transfers facilitated by the historical Silk Road.
questions.sample_answer: The Silk Road enabled the spread of Buddhism from India into East Asia via oasis kingdoms, and transferred papermaking technology from Tang Dynasty China to the Islamic world after the Battle of Talas in 751 CE.

title: Functional Programming with Java Streams & Lambdas
question: Write a Java class OrderAnalytics that processes a collection of Order objects using the Stream API to filter completed orders, group by customer region, calculate average order value, and return the top 3 highest spending customers.
evaluation_criteria: Correct usage of stream pipelines: filter, map, collect
Implementation of Collectors.groupingBy and Collectors.averagingDouble
Proper handling of null values and defensive stream closing

questions.prompt: Provide the stream pipeline that groups orders by customer and sums their total spend.
questions.sample_answer: orders.stream().filter(Order::isCompleted).collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Order::getCustomerId, Collectors.summingDouble(Order::getAmount)));

title: Building a Robust Custom Thread Pool Executor
question: Implement a minimal custom worker thread pool in Java using a BlockingQueue, fixed worker threads, graceful shutdown mechanisms, and rejected execution policies.
evaluation_criteria: Thread safe task queue management using BlockingQueue
Worker loop handling InterruptedException and task execution
Implementation of shutdown() and awaitTermination() lifecycle states

questions.prompt: Explain how worker threads continuously fetch and execute tasks from the blocking queue.
questions.sample_answer: Worker threads run a loop calling queue.take(), which blocks until a task is available, executes task.run(), catches RuntimeExceptions to prevent thread termination, and exits only when an interrupted shutdown signal is detected.

title: Custom Memoization Decorator with TTL Expiration
question: Develop a Python decorator @timed_lru_cache(maxsize=128, ttl_seconds=60) that caches function return values for given arguments and invalidates entries after their time-to-live expires. Use functools.wraps.
evaluation_criteria: Use of functools.wraps to preserve function metadata
Dictionary cache storing tuples of (result, timestamp)
Correct eviction logic when cache exceeds maxsize or TTL expires

questions.prompt: Write the wrapper function implementation for the time-aware caching decorator.

title: Self-Balancing AVL Tree Implementation
question: Implement insertion into an AVL Tree. Code the left rotation, right rotation, left-right double rotation, and right-left double rotation methods while maintaining balance factors within {-1, 0, 1}.
evaluation_criteria: Height recalculation logic after insertions
Accurate implementation of left and right single rotations
Correct resolution of all 4 imbalance cases (LL, RR, LR, RL)

questions.prompt: Provide the code for a single right rotation (LL rotation) on an unbalanced node.
questions.sample_answer:
def rotate_right(y):
    x = y.left
    T2 = x.right
    x.right = y
    y.left = T2
    y.height = 1 + max(get_height(y.left), get_height(y.right))
    x.height = 1 + max(get_height(x.left), get_height(x.right))
    return x

evaluation_criteria: Adjacency list representation of weighted directed graphs
Correct relaxation step: if dist[u] + weight < dist[v]
Predecessor pointer array to reconstruct the full path from source to target

questions.prompt: Demonstrate the heap relaxation step in Dijkstra's algorithm.

evaluation_criteria: Clean separation of Server and Client Components ('use client' boundaries)
Utilization of Suspense streaming with custom fallback skeletons
Server action handling input validation and revalidatePath('/analytics')
